([[Tilton, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] (2015–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 48 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | career_start = 2019 | years1 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years2 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team2 = →[[Agua Caliente Clippers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team3 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team4 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | highlights = }} '''Terance Stanley Mann''' (born October 18, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. Mann was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 48th overall pick. Mann played six seasons with the Clippers before being traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2025. ==Early life== Mann was born in [[Brooklyn]], New York and moved to [[Lowell, Massachusetts]] at the age of 10.{{Cite news |last=Langone |first=Matt |date=November 8, 2017 |title=Lowell native Mann stars for Florida State |url=http://www.lowellsun.com/sports/ci_31438622/soaring-seminole |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Lowell Sun]]}} His parents are from [[Saint Lucia]].{{cite web |title=Chris Boucher and Terance Mann could be key in developing St. Lucia's basketball |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/chris-boucher-and-terance-mann-could-be-key-in-developing-st-lucia-s-basketball |website=FIBA |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=November 14, 2019}} Mann's mother, [[Daynia La-Force]], coached women's basketball at [[Rhode Island Rams women's basketball|Rhode Island]].{{cite news |last=Deen |first=Safid |title=FSU forward Terance Mann credits mother for turning him into strong leader, floor coach |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-state-seminoles/chopping-block/os-sp-fsu-terance-mann-1112-story.html |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=November 11, 2017}} He played for the [[Hillside School (Marlborough, Massachusetts)|Hillside School]] in Massachusetts and the [[Tilton School]] in New Hampshire.{{cite web |last= Sullivan|first= Maureen|date= March 1, 2024|title= Hillside honors NBA star, alum Terance Mann|url= https://www.communityadvocate.com/education/hillside-honors-nba-star-alum-terance-mann/article_87ebc188-a2e7-5a83-84a4-eed967df2b97.html|website= Community Advocate|location= [[Westborough, Massachusetts]]|publisher= |access-date= August 25, 2026}} At Tilton School, he averaged 23.1 points and 7.8 rebounds per game as a senior. He led the school to a 31–5 record and the New England Preparatory School Athletic Conference Class AA championship. Mann was a First Team All-NEPSAC selection.{{cite news |title=New Hampshire Boys Basketball POY: Terance Mann |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/gatorade-new-hampshire-boys-basketball-poy-terance-mann |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=March 20, 2015}} Mann was a four-star recruit and signed with Florida State, turning down offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]]. ==College career== As a freshman at Florida State, Mann averaged 5.2 points and 17.0 minutes per game playing behind [[Malik Beasley]] and [[Dwayne Bacon]]. He was named a captain as a sophomore and posted 8.4 points and 4.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last=Weiler |first=Curt |title=The evolution of Florida State 'stat stuffer' Terance Mann |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/football/2019/03/04/terance-mann-florida-state-fsu-mens-basketball-senior-day-leonard-hamilton-charlton-young-seminoles/3056238002/ |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=March 4, 2019}} Mann came down with a torn abdominal and groin muscle in the first round of the 2017 NCAA Tournament and was limited as the Seminoles reached the Elite Eight.{{cite news |last=Holton |first=Brooks |title=Terance Mann: 3 things to know about Florida State basketball's senior guard |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2018/12/01/terance-mann-fsu-florida-state-seminoles-mens-basketball-facts-know/2160698002/ |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=December 6, 2018}} Mann posted 12.6 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game as a junior.{{cite news |last=Keel |first=Fletcher |title=Fans: Mann most likely to get drafted in 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://www.wctv.tv/content/news/FAN-OPINION-Mann-most-likely-to-get-drafted-in-2019-NBA-Draft-486896001.html |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=WCTV |date=June 28, 2018}} As a senior, Mann averaged 11.4 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. He led the team to a 29–8 record and the Sweet Sixteen of the NCAA Tournament.{{cite news |last=McGahee |first=Wayne |title=What will Florida State men's basketball look like next season? |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2019/03/29/florida-state-fsu-mens-basketball-2019-2020-preview-mfiondu-kabengele-trent-forrest-leonard-hamilton/3309603002/ |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=March 29, 2019}} He finished his career as the third player in school history with over 1,200 points, 600 rebounds, 200 assists and 100 steals. ==Professional career== === Los Angeles Clippers (2019–2025) === Mann was drafted with the 48th pick of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |last=Ibarra |first=Joseph |date=June 20, 2019 |title=L.A. Clippers Select Terance Mann with 48th Overall Pick in 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-select-terance-mann-48th-overall-pick-2019-nba-draft |access-date=June 20, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} He played for the Clippers in the 2019 [[NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Miguel |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Summer League Recap Clippers vs. Lakers |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/summer-league-recap-clippers-vs-lakers |access-date=August 7, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Miguel |date=July 7, 2019 |title=Summer League Recap Clippers vs. Grizzlies |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/summer-league-recap-clippers-vs-grizzlies |access-date=August 7, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2019 |title=Clippers' Terance Mann: Records near triple-double |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-terance-mann-records-near-triple-double/ |access-date=August 7, 2023 |website=cbssports.com}} On July 9, 2019, the Clippers announced that they had signed Mann.{{cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Miguel |date=July 9, 2019 |title=L.A. Clippers Sign Kabengele and Mann |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/rookie-signing-prep |access-date=July 9, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} On October 24, 2019, Mann made his NBA debut, coming off the bench in a 141–122 win over the [[2019–20 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] with a rebound.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160658|title=Now with Clippers, Kawhi Leonard spoils Warriors fun again|date=October 24, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 24, 2019}} On March 18, 2020, the Clippers announced that Mann had undergone surgery to repair a ligament in his right hand.{{cite web |last=Dixon |first=Robyn |date=March 18, 2020 |title=Terance Mann Undergoes Hand Surgery |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/terance-mann-undergoes-hand-surgery |access-date=March 18, 2020 |website=NBA.com}} On August 14, 2020, in a game against the [[2019–20 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]], Mann recorded a then-career-high 25 points, 14 rebounds and nine assists in 42 minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/sports/terance-mann-leads-clippers-over-thunder-as-stars-rest-for-playoffs/2413300/|title=Terance Mann Leads Clippers Over Thunder as Stars Rest for Playoffs|website=NBC|date=August 13, 2020|access-date=June 19, 2021}} During the 2021 Western Conference Semifinals, with [[Kawhi Leonard]] being injured, Mann was put in the starting lineup. In game 6, Mann dropped a career-high 39 points on 7-of-10 shooting from three-point range in a 131–119 victory, sparking a 25-point comeback and leading the Clippers to the [[NBA Conference Finals|Western Conference Finals]] for the first time in franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/clippers-news-paul-georges-immediate-reaction-to-terance-manns-shocking-game-6/|title=VIDEO: Clippers star Paul George's immediate reaction to Terance Mann's shocking Game 6|website=ClutchPoints|last=Salao|first=Renzo|date=June 18, 2021|access-date=June 18, 2021}} On October 12, 2021, Mann signed a two-year, $22 million contract extension.{{cite web |date=October 12, 2021 |title=LA Clippers guard Terance Mann agrees to two-year, $22 million contract extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32388022/the-la-clippers-guard-terance-mann-agrees-two-year-22-million-contract-extension |access-date=April 17, 2026 |publisher=espn.com}} On January 15, 2023, Mann scored a season-high 31 points during a 121–100 win over the [[2022–23 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].{{Cite magazine |last=Bowles |first=Charleston |date=January 17, 2023 |title=Terance Mann sets new regular season career high in victory |url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/pro-noles/terance-mann-sets-new-regular-season-career-high-in-victory |access-date=August 7, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} On September 27, 2024, Mann agreed to a three-year, $47 million contract extension with the Clippers.{{Cite web |last=Youngmisuk |first=Ohm |date=September 27, 2024 |title=Sources: Clippers, Terance Mann agree on 3-year, $47M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41480152 |access-date=October 3, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} === Atlanta Hawks (2025) === On February 6, 2025, Mann and [[Bones Hyland]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for guard [[Bogdan Bogdanović (basketball)|Bogdan Bogdanović]], and three second-round draft picks.{{cite web |date=February 6, 2025 |title=Atlanta Hawks Receive Terance Mann and Nah'Shon "Bones" Hyland from LA Clippers |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-receive-terance-mann-and-nahshon-bones-hyland-from-la-clippers |access-date=December 6, 2025 |work=NBA.com}} On February 26, 2025, Mann recorded 13 points, 4 rebounds and 4 assists while coming off the bench in a 131–109 loss against the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/videos/terance-mann-provides-13-pts-4-reb-4-ast-off-bench-in-hawks-loss-in-miami |title=Terance Mann provides 13 PTS, 4 REB, & 4 AST off bench in Hawks loss in Miami |language=en |access-date=2025-06-25 |via=NBA.com}} On March 10, 2025, Mann would have of his best games with the Hawks in which he recorded a team-high 19 points along with 6 rebounds and 4 assists in 33 minutes of action off the bench in a 132–123 win against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |date=2025-03-11 |title=76ers vs Hawks Game Highlights |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/video/76ers-vs-hawks-game-highlights-021446453.html |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} On April 13, 2025, during the final game of the regular season, Mann was put in the [[starting lineup]] for the first time as a member of the Hawks in which he tied his team-high 19 points, while recording 4 assists and 3 rebounds in a 117–105 win against the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Clement |date=April 16, 2005 |title=Hawks finish regular season strong, fall in first play-in game |url=https://www.emorywheel.com/article/2025/04/hawks-finish-regular-season-strong-fall-in-first-play-in-game |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=The Emory Wheel |language=en-US}} === Brooklyn Nets (2025–present) === On July 7, 2025, Mann and the draft rights to [[Drake Powell]] (the 22nd pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]]) were traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a three-team trade that sent the [[Boston Celtics]]' [[Kristaps Porziņģis]] and a second-round pick to the Hawks, and [[Georges Niang]] and a second-round pick to the Celtics.{{Cite web |date=2025-07-07 |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Terance Mann and Draft Rights to Drake Powell in Three-Team Trade |url=https://brooklynnets.com/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-terance-mann-and-draft-rights-to-drake-powell-in-three-team-trade |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=brooklynnets.com |language=en}} ==Executive career== On April 4, 2025, Mann was hired to serve as the assistant general manager for his alma mater, [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], under new head coach [[Luke Loucks]].{{Cite web |date=April 4, 2025 |title=Loucks Adds Terance Mann As Assistant General Manager |url=https://seminoles.com/news/2025/4/4/mens-basketball-loucks-adds-terance-mann-as-assistant-general-manager |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=seminoles.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics==
